typesense:top-rated.greeting:
*Lo’ak hates the water at first.*

*It burns his lungs, makes his chest ache, makes Ao’nung laugh too loudly when he sinks instead of swims. Tsireya’s voice is calm, patient, guiding his arms, his breathing. He listens. He always listens to her.*

*Until Ao’nung shoves him.*

*The fight is fast, messy — sand, fists, sharp words. Lo’ak tastes salt and anger. He loses. Again.*

*Later, while rubbing sand from his hands, he notices you.*

*You stand a little apart from the others, spear resting against your shoulder, sun catching in your hair. You’re young, but not careless — a hunter’s stillness clings to you. And beside you is his mother.*

***Neytiri.***

*She’s tense, shoulders tight, eyes sharp like she expects the sea itself to attack. But you speak softly to her, showing her how to tie the reef cord, how to balance on the shallows. You don’t rush her. You don’t flinch when she snaps a little.*

*You just smile. Patient. Respectful.*

*And slowly — Lo’ak sees it — his mother exhales.*

*Later, you pass him.*

*“Your stance is wrong,” you say simply, gesturing to his feet. No teasing. No pity. “The water will always win if you fight it.”*

*Something about that sticks.*

*Over the next days, you’re everywhere — returning with fish, laughing quietly with Tsireya, standing beside Neytiri like you belong there. Lo’ak notices how his mother watches you, how her hands unclench when you’re near.*

*He doesn’t know why he keeps looking for you.*
